main_result: Let T_10 = conv(0,e_1,...,e_10) in R^10 and K = T_10 x T_10 in R^20. With R_d(K) = |Pi K|/|K|^{d-1} and c_d = (d+1)d^d/d!, the paper claims R_20(K)/c_20 = 121*C(20,10)/(21*2^20) = 22355476/22020096 > 1, so K violates the proposed simplex bound |Pi K| <= c_d |K|^{d-1} (Brannen's conjecture) in dimension 20. The mechanism is the product identity R_{r+s}(A x B) = R_r(A) R_s(B) for polytopes. A secondary corollary gives, for some lambda>1 and all large n, a product of simplices K_n in R^n with R_n(K_n)/R_n(T_n) >= lambda^n. I checked the arithmetic: 121*184756 = 22355476, 21*1048576 = 22020096, the difference 335380 is correct, the closed form for c_10 = 17187500/567 is correct, and A = 2^22*5^8/(567*11^9) is about 1.2254 > 1. The formula for the product test and the bound c_n < (n+1)e^n < (n+1)(11/4)^n also check out.
proof_strategy: Lemma (facets) writes the projection body of a polytope as a zonotope: h_{Pi P}(u) = (1/2) sum_F s_F |<nu_F,u>|, obtained from a double-counting argument on the projection of the polytope. Proposition (product) uses that facets of A x B are of the form F x B or A x G, so the area-normal vectors separate into the two factors and the support functions add. Lemma (affine) shows Pi(LP) = |det L| L^{-t} Pi P for polytopes via the transformation of facet areas, then extends to general convex bodies by approximation with inscribed polytopes. Proposition (simplex) computes |Pi T_d| as the volume of a translate of (cube + segment)/(d-1)!, using a Fubini fiber argument and h_{Pi Q}(w) = d for the cube, which gives R_d(T_d) = c_d. The theorem is then exact arithmetic on c_10^2/c_20. The corollary bounds c_n by (n+1)(11/4)^n, writes each n as 10k + d_r, and uses the product T_10^k x T_{d_r}, so the ratio grows like (A/lambda^10)^k.
hardest_part: The least-verified part is the general-convex-body approximation in Lemma (affine): the sandwich P_m subset P subset P_m + eps B, the claim that the increasing sequence can be chosen, and the passage to the limit that yields covariance for arbitrary bodies. The main theorem only uses polytopes, so this step is not needed for the counterexample itself. Also, the measure-zero argument in the facet formula is stated more than it is proved. I did verify the closed-form arithmetic, the simplex volume computation, and the product identity by hand.

main_result: Let T_d be the standard d-simplex, with |T_d|=1/d!, and let R_d(K)=|ΠK|/|K|^{d-1}. The manuscript claims R_d(T_d)=c_d=(d+1)d^d/d!, and that K=T_10×T_10 in R^20 satisfies R_20(K)/c_20 = 121·C(20,10)/(21·2^20) = 22355476/22020096 > 1, so K violates the proposed simplex upper bound |ΠK| ≤ c_d|K|^{d-1} in dimension 20. A second result (Corollary) gives λ>1 and N such that for n≥N some product of simplices K_n⊂R^n has R_n(K_n)/R_n(T_n) ≥ λ^n. I checked the main algebra independently: c_2=6 matches a direct zonotope area computation; the simplex projection body volume (d+1)/((d-1)!)^d, the product identity, the closed form for R_20/c_20 with the integer certificate 335380, c_10=17187500/567, and A=1638400000000/1336956340797 > 1 all check out.
proof_strategy: The proof has three layers. Lemma 1 writes the projection body of a polytope as a zonotope, Π P = sum over facets of centered segments [-s_F ν_F/2, s_F ν_F/2], via the Cauchy projection formula with multiplicity two. Proposition 2 splits the facets of A×B into F×B and A×G, which gives Π(A×B) = (|B|ΠA)×(|A|ΠB) and hence the multiplicativity R_{r+s}(A×B)=R_r(A)R_s(B). Lemma 3 gives affine covariance of Π (and invariance of R_d) first for polytopes, then extends to convex bodies by polytope approximation. Proposition 4 computes the simplex: its facet normals give Π T_d as a translate of ([0,1]^d+[0,w])/(d-1)!, and a Fubini/extrusion argument gives |[0,1]^d+[0,w]|=d+1. The main theorem is then arithmetic on c_10^2/c_20 using the product identity, and the corollary uses bounds c_n<(n+1)β^n with β=11/4 and a residue-class argument in k.
hardest_part: The least-verified part is the convex-body approximation in Lemma 3 (affine covariance). The sandwich estimates and the uniform convergence of support functions are plausible, but the existence and nesting of the inscribed polytopes P_m and the passage of the covariance identity to the limit are only sketched. The facet-formula measure-zero argument in Lemma 1 is also terse. The numerical claims in the main theorem and corollary I could redo, and they are correct; the final corollary's threshold argument is logically sound once the displayed lower bound holds.

main_result: Theorem 1: for T_10 = conv(0,e_1,...,e_10) in R^10 and K = T_10 x T_10 in R^20, R_20(K)/c_20 = 121*binom(20,10)/(21*2^20) = 22355476/22020096 > 1, where R_d(K) = |Pi K|/|K|^{d-1} and c_d = (d+1)d^d/d!. So K violates the proposed simplex bound |Pi K| <= c_d |K|^{d-1} in dimension 20. Supporting results: (i) a product identity R_{r+s}(A x B) = R_r(A) R_s(B) for full-dimensional polytopes; (ii) R_d(T_d) = c_d and all full-dimensional simplices share this value; (iii) Corollary: with fixed lambda > 1, some product of simplices K_n in R^n satisfies R_n(K_n)/R_n(T_n) >= lambda^n for all large n. I checked the arithmetic: c_10 = 17187500/567, the ratio identity, binom(20,10)=184756, 121*184756 = 22355476, 21*2^20 = 22020096, the difference 335380, the general product-test formula, and the constant A = c_10/(11/4)^10 = 1638400000000/1336956340797 > 1 (after cancelling a factor 11 from 11^10 and the numerator). I also checked c_d = (d+1)d^{d-1}/(d-1)! for the simplex, the d=2 case (|Pi T_2| = 3, R_2 = 6), and the bound c_n < (n+1)e^n < (n+1)(11/4)^n. I found no false statement; the issues below are gaps in justification, bookkeeping and notation.
proof_strategy: The proof has three layers. Lemma 2 (facet formula) gives h_{Pi P}(u) = (1/2) sum_F s_F |<nu_F,u>|, so Pi P is a zonotope built from the facet area-normal vectors. Proposition 3 (product) uses this: the facets of A x B are F x B and A x G, so Pi(A x B) = (|B| Pi A) x (|A| Pi B), and the normalized volume ratio multiplies. Proposition 5 (simplex) computes the facet area-normal vectors of T_d, identifies Pi T_d with a dilate of the zonotope [0,1]^d + [0,w], and uses a Fubini/fiber argument (|Q+[0,w]| = 1 + h_{Pi Q}(w) = d+1) to obtain |Pi T_d| = (d+1)/((d-1)!)^d and then R_d(T_d) = c_d. The main theorem is then exact arithmetic on R_10(T_10)^2 / c_20. The corollary takes products T_10^k x T_{d_r}, bounds c_n by (n+1)(11/4)^n, and shows the ratio to lambda^n tends to infinity in k for lambda < A^{1/10}. The affine covariance lemma for general convex bodies (approximation by polytopes) is not needed for the main counterexample, which uses only polytopes.
hardest_part: The least trustworthy part for me is the generic-line/measure-zero argument in the proof of the facet formula (Lemma 2), and the prism/height step in the affine covariance proof, both of which are only sketched. I verified the final formulas by recomputing them, and the main counterexample depends only on the facet formula for simplices, the product identity, and exact arithmetic, all of which I could check. The approximation argument for general convex bodies is the part I checked least closely, though the main result does not depend on it.
